item.title: One big JSON.parse and every request waits: the Node.js event loop in practice
item.description: Coming to Node from Java, the concurrency model is the thing that takes longest to really feel. In a Spring Boot service, a slow request blocks its own thread, and the other two hundred threads carry on. In Node there’s one thread running your JavaScript. If one request keeps it busy for 800 ms, every other request on that process waits 800 ms. Your p99 latency goes up for everybody, and the slow request isn’t even the one that looks slow in the logs.
